gaps.sentence: The success of the launch rests on the ___ (RELY) of the supplier.
gaps.explanation: 'The reliability of the supplier' — the quality noun is needed after 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He ___ denied knowing anything about the plan (FIRM).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'denied': firmly. Note the doubled m before -ly.

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The vaccine is still awaiting official ___ (APPROVE).
gaps.explanation: 'Official approval' — the noun form follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The island is ___ , with no permanent residents (HABIT).
gaps.explanation: 'No permanent residents' shows the negative: uninhabited (un- + inhabited). An adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: The article was full of ___ information (ACCURATE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'information'
gaps.explanation: The negative adjective 'inaccurate' (in- + accurate) modifies the noun 'information'.
